article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Sour D × HashBurger
Breeder: California Seedbank
THC Content: 24-26%
CBD Content: Low to trace
Terpene Profile: beta-caryophyllene , limonene , and myrcene
Primary Flavors: Sour diesel, lemon citrus, garlic, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Sour HashBurger brings together two sides of cannabis that rarely need an introduction: the sharp, unmistakable fuel of Sour Diesel and the greasy, savory resin production of the modern Burger family. California Seedbank created the cultivar by crossing Sour D with HashBurger, producing a feminized indica-leaning hybrid with an official flowering window of roughly eight to nine weeks. Its appeal is less about fruit-candy sweetness than sheer aromatic force. Properly grown flower can move from sour lemon and petroleum into garlic, skunk, damp earth, pepper, and an almost hash-like richness as the buds are broken apart.

The experience follows an equally layered trajectory, beginning with enough cerebral energy to keep the strain from feeling immediately heavy before the HashBurger influence gradually adds a broader physical calm. For growers and hash enthusiasts, however, perhaps the most important part of the pedigree is resin. HashBurger was deliberately selected by California Seedbank for abundant trichome production and solventless extraction performance, qualities that make its Sour Diesel offspring particularly interesting to cultivators looking for weed that performs both as premium flower and as raw material for hash.
Genetics and Lineage

California Seedbank lists Sour HashBurger simply and clearly as Sour D × HashBurger. The cross was produced by Mr. and Mrs. Respect, the breeders behind California Seedbank and the original HashBurger. Sour Diesel brings the brighter half of the equation. Its classic character revolves around piercing fuel, sour citrus, pine, and a cerebral cannabis experience that has helped keep Diesel genetics relevant for decades. Rather than allowing that parent to stand alone, the breeders paired it with a much heavier contemporary resin line, giving the finished hybrid more density, savory funk, and physical depth.

HashBurger has a particularly elaborate pedigree. California Seedbank identifies the original plant as Han Solo Hash Plant × Double Burger. Han Solo Hash Plant itself combines Han Solo Burger and Black Triangle Kush, while Double Burger brings GMO and Donny Burger genetics into the family tree. This explains why Sour HashBurger can smell considerably more complicated than the name suggests. Sour Diesel contributes acidic fuel and citrus, while the Burger side introduces garlic, onion-like funk, skunk, Kush earthiness, and thick resin production. The result is not merely Sour Diesel with heavier buds; it is a collision between an old-school American gas profile and a newer generation of cannabis selected specifically for loud terpenes and hash-making potential.
Effects and Experience

Sour HashBurger tends to make the Diesel portion of its ancestry apparent early in the session. The initial shift is generally more cerebral than the indica-leaning classification might imply, with an elevated mood and increased mental engagement developing before deep physical heaviness. Music, conversation, creative projects, or low-pressure activities can feel more interesting as the head high establishes itself. The sour, pungent aroma can also make the strain feel psychologically stimulating before the full body component becomes evident.

That energy does not usually remain the entire story. As the session continues, the HashBurger side adds a heavier physical dimension that can soften muscle tension and make sitting still increasingly attractive. Rather than producing an abrupt transition into sedation, the high often feels as though its center of gravity gradually moves downward from the head into the body. Moderate amounts may remain suitable for experienced consumers who want to relax without becoming immediately inactive, whereas large servings are more likely to produce substantial heaviness. Strong THC-rich marijuana can also cause dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, anxiety, or temporary difficulty concentrating, making dose control especially important for people with lower tolerance.
Medical Benefits

The combination of cerebral uplift and physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana patients looking for a strain that sits between highly stimulating daytime cannabis and deeply sedating nighttime varieties. Some consumers may select this type of profile when dealing with temporary stress, reduced appetite, tension, or discomfort that becomes more noticeable toward the end of the day. The gradually increasing body effect may also appeal to people who want to unwind without beginning the experience with immediate drowsiness.

Sour HashBurger itself has not been clinically studied as a treatment for pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or other medical conditions, so strain-specific therapeutic claims would be inappropriate. Its cannabinoid and terpene composition can also change considerably between phenotypes and cultivation environments. Medical users should therefore look at the certificate of analysis for the actual flower or concentrate being purchased instead of assuming every batch carries the same THC or terpene percentages. People using prescription medication or managing significant medical conditions should discuss high-THC cannabis use with a qualified healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The nose is unapologetically pungent. Sour Diesel provides an immediate blast of gasoline and tart citrus, while the HashBurger genetics fill the space beneath it with garlic, skunk, earth, and savory funk. California Seedbank describes the original HashBurger parent as carrying intensely skunky, fuel-forward aromatics, and those characteristics fit naturally alongside Sour D’s sharper profile. Breaking apart a resinous flower can release lemon peel and pine before the heavier Burger notes arrive, creating an aroma that is bright at the edges but dark and almost greasy through the center.

Flavor develops in stages rather than presenting one dominant note from start to finish. Sour lemon and diesel are typically the most obvious elements on the inhale. Peppery spice and pine can emerge through the middle, followed by earth, garlic, and lingering skunk on the exhale. Depending on phenotype, the savory side may range from subtle background funk to a powerful GMO-like character. This is not weed designed primarily for consumers chasing berries, candy, or creamy dessert flavors. Its appeal is rooted in the older vocabulary of cannabis—gas, skunk, sour citrus, soil, garlic, and hash—presented through contemporary resin-heavy genetics.
Growing Information

California Seedbank sells Sour HashBurger as a feminized photoperiod cultivar and gives an official indoor flowering period of approximately eight to nine weeks. The genetic pairing should offer considerable vigor, with the Sour D side encouraging stretch and lateral branching while HashBurger contributes dense flower development and extensive trichome coverage. Growers should anticipate more vertical movement after the light cycle is changed than they would from a compact pure indica. Topping, low-stress training, and an organized trellis can help spread branches across the canopy before flowering stretch becomes difficult to manage.

Resin production is one of the strongest reasons to cultivate this hybrid carefully. California Seedbank reports that the original HashBurger can produce exceptionally large solventless returns and describes it as a vigorous, high-yielding plant with heavily trichome-coated flowers. Sour HashBurger was developed within the same Burger breeding program, making healthy flower development and resin preservation particularly important. During late bloom, strong airflow should reach both the canopy and interior branches because thick flowers can trap moisture. Growers should also avoid excessive nitrogen late in flowering, which can interfere with maturation and finished flower quality.

Outdoors, a sunny location with ample root space should allow the branching structure to develop more fully. An eight-to-nine-week flowering duration places a likely finish around late September or early October in many Northern Hemisphere environments, although latitude and phenotype can alter the schedule substantially. Heavy branches may need stakes or trellising as flowers gain weight. Once harvested, a controlled drying period is essential; excessive heat or rapid drying can strip away the volatile sour-lemon and fuel notes that distinguish the strain from more generic gas-heavy marijuana.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Sour HashBurger?

Sour HashBurger is Sour D × HashBurger. California Seedbank lists that exact lineage for its feminized release. The HashBurger parent is itself Han Solo Hash Plant × Double Burger, giving the strain a substantial background of Burger, GMO, Kush, and hash-oriented genetics.
Who bred Sour HashBurger?
California Seedbank bred Sour HashBurger. The company is operated by breeders Mr. and Mrs. Respect, who also created the original HashBurger used as one of the parents in this cross.
Is Sour HashBurger indica or sativa?

California Seedbank classifies it as an indica hybrid. The effects can nevertheless begin with a relatively energetic cerebral character inherited from Sour Diesel before becoming more relaxing and physically weighted as the session develops.
What does Sour HashBurger taste like?

Expect sour diesel and lemon citrus at the front of the profile, followed by pine, pepper, garlic, earth, skunk, and savory gas. Phenotypes expressing more HashBurger influence may develop stronger garlic and funky notes, while Sour D-dominant plants can emphasize acidic citrus and fuel.
How long does Sour HashBurger take to flower?

The breeder lists an indoor flowering period of approximately eight to nine weeks. Actual harvest timing should still be determined by flower maturity and trichome development rather than cutting automatically on a specific day.
Final Thoughts on Sour HashBurger

Sour HashBurger is a strong example of how modern breeders can revisit classic marijuana genetics without simply reproducing them. California Seedbank took the unmistakable fuel and citrus identity of Sour D and placed it against HashBurger, a cultivar built from several layers of Burger, GMO, Kush, and hash-focused breeding. The result preserves the sharp personality associated with Diesel while adding thicker flowers, savory funk, and the type of resin production that has made the Burger family attractive to solventless extractors.

What separates this cultivar from the flood of sweet modern hybrids is its commitment to pungency. Sour lemon, petroleum, garlic, pine, earth, and skunk dominate a profile that feels intentionally loud rather than polished into candy sweetness. Add an effect that can begin bright and cerebral before settling into heavier relaxation, and Sour HashBurger becomes useful for more than its impressive pedigree. For cannabis consumers who miss aggressively sour, fuel-driven weed—and for growers interested in resin-rich genetics capable of producing serious flower or hash—the strain represents a compelling bridge between classic Sour Diesel character and the modern Burger era.
